transcript:
Meeting header - 2027-05-04 11:00am PT | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jamal (Redwood SE), Olivia Chen (Head of Platform, Helion), Mateo Ruiz (Lead ML Eng), Samir Patel (CTO)
Location: Video call. Recording start.

Auto-summary (auto): Helion exploring Redwood for customer-facing assistants and search. Focus on integration path: how SDKs fit into existing LangChain/LlamaIndex pipelines, where to place a gateway/proxy, and how to enforce quotas and observability for billing and SLOs.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out the time. quick intro from our side — i'm maya, account lead, and jamal here is our solutions engineer — jamal do you want to say hi?
[00:07] Jamal: hey, yeah hey all. jamal reynolds, lead se on infra and integrations, i usually sit in on gateway, batching, and private deployments.
[00:14] Olivia: thanks, i'm olivia. head of platform at helion, i run the infra teams and own the integration roadmap. excited to hear how you handle multi-tenant routing.
[00:22] Samir: samir here, cto, short on time today — mainly listening for procurement/security flags.
[00:27] Mateo: and i'm mateo, lead ml eng, i work on our LangChain pipelines and embeddings infra.

[00:34] Maya: awesome. high-level: you mentioned in the intake form that you're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for a production pilot. do you want to walk us through the constraints?
[00:42] Olivia: yeah, so our P0 is to ship a chat assistant on our storefront that does product recs + returns guidance. latency target is sub-400ms for p95 if possible. we also have firm data residency requirements in eu-west for a subset of traffic. security is a blocker for external pii — we need encryption, audit logs, and sso. lastly, cost matters; we want to compare hosted pricing vs dedicated pool.
[01:05] Jamal: great. sub-400 p95 is aggressive but doable depending on model and batching. are you planning to run open models or a managed model?
[01:12] Mateo: primarily open Llama variants for cost control, maybe a small commercial model for higher-quality cases. we currently orchestrate calls through LangChain and store embeddings with LlamaIndex for retrieval.
[01:22] Maya: helpful. two threads i'll call out. one — integration path: do you want Redwood SDKs embedded in your app, or a gateway/proxy approach that all services hit? two — deployment: hosted for easiest start, dedicated for reserved capacity + isolation, private for VPC/on-prem when compliance demands it.
[01:40] Olivia: curious about the gateway option. we have a central API gateway today; would it be better to call Redwood from each service or front it with a proxy?
[01:48] Jamal: both patterns are common. proxy/gateway allows central rate limiting, multi-tenant routing, and token accounting at the edge. our recommended pattern for Helion's use-case — where you want consistent enforcement and observability — is a lightweight edge proxy that attaches tenant headers and routes to Redwood Dedicated pools or the hosted endpoint depending on policy. the other route is SDKs embedded in services which gives lower latency but requires each service to implement retry/fallbacks and token metrics.
[02:14] Mateo: so for LangChain/LlamaIndex, how would that map? we already have chains that call out to openai-ish abstractions — can we swap in Redwood without refactoring a ton?
[02:24] Jamal: yes. our SDKs expose a compatible interface with common libraries. we have sample connectors for LangChain and a LlamaIndex adapter — i'll share repo links after. typical pattern is to implement a Redwood client as the LLM wrapper and use the same prompt templates. a subtle point — streaming and function calls need slight glue, but nothing major.
[02:42] Olivia: what about rate limits and quotas? we need hard quotas per tenant and burst protection so a single storefront doesn't blow up our bill.
[02:49] Jamal: we support route-level rate limits and quota tokens. you can configure token quotas per api key or tenant id, and we emit X-RateLimit headers for latency-aware clients. for hard enforcement, you can set denials or fallback to a cheaper model variant. also, for Dedicated you can configure burst capacity and autoscale limits.
[03:09] Samir: is that per-second QPS limits or token-based? we charge partners by token so we want token-level accounting surfaced to billing.
[03:16] Jamal: both. we do both QPS and token quotas. our observability exposes per-request token counts, model chosen, and latency breakdown. that feeds into the console's cost reports so finance can map to tenant usage.
[03:26] Mateo: nice. about KV cache and prefix caching — we rely heavily on assume-chachy? [laughs] — on long conversations. do you have a shared KV cache for response reuse?
[03:37] Jamal: yep — our runtime supports KV cache for attention and prefix caching to reduce repeated compute, especially for long chat sessions. we also have automatic prefix caching heuristics for repeated prompts which can drop token costs a lot. note: sometimes the transcriber might say KV "cash" — but it's KV cache.
[03:51] Olivia: haha noted. security — we need KMS integration and audit logs shipped to our SIEM. can Redwood talk to our KMS or HSM?
[03:59] Maya: yes. Private deployments can integrate with your KMS; Dedicated has options to use customer-managed keys for data-at-rest. we also provide structured audit logs and can stream to your syslog/Splunk or S3. i'll attach our SOC 2 and KMS guide after.
[04:13] Samir: for PCI/PII reasons, we might require VPC-only egress for production. does Private imply on-prem or VPC peering?
[04:21] Jamal: Private is flexible — VPC peering for cloud region deployments or an on-prem package if you need air-gapped. either way you keep the control plane separate per tenant. there's a tradeoff: private reduces our ability to route load globally, but gains in isolation and compliance.
[04:36] Mateo: about SDK language support — we use Python for LangChain and Node for a few edge services. what libs are first-class?
[04:43] Jamal: Python and Node SDKs are first-class, and we have example LangChain wrapper, LlamaIndex connector, and a small Node middleware for express/fastify. we also publish sample Docker sidecar for proxy mode. i'll drop the links.
[04:56] Olivia: do you have an opinion on where to place the reranker — in the gateway or in the model pool? we're doing semantic search with embeddings then rerank with a small generative model.
[05:05] Jamal: rerank can live in the model pool as a call after retrieval, or you can do it closer to retrieval if you want to reduce latency with a cached small model. the gateway can orchestrate multi-call flows and even stitch embeddings results to the model call using our tracing hooks so you can see per-step latency.
[05:22] Maya: quick interjection — are there any blockers from a procurement/timing standpoint that we should know?
[05:28] Samir: timeline wise, procurement wants a vendor that supports SOC 2 and SSO. they also want to know if Private will require a separate contract. if hosted is acceptable for pilot then procurement is faster. what's the usual timeline?
[05:40] Maya: for a hosted pilot it's usually a few days for trial creds and a week for basic integration. Dedicated typically takes 2–4 weeks for capacity reservation and network setup. Private/on-prem can be 6–8 weeks depending on networking and security reviews.
[05:53] Olivia: okay. for pilot we prefer lowest friction. can we start with hosted for a subset of traffic and then graduate to Dedicated?
[05:59] Jamal: absolutely — we do that a lot. you can pin model versions, then move traffic to a Dedicated pool when you want strict isolation. key is to design the gateway to be policy-aware so you can flip routing rules without changing app code.
[06:11] Mateo: performance bench — can we get a small test harness? we need to validate p95 under a bursty storefront load (50 concurrent users with 200ms think time).
[06:21] Jamal: yes — i'll provide a simple load script that hits the SDK and the proxy. we'll instrument it to capture token counts and per-request traces. recommended approach: run a 1-hour baseline, then a 10-minute spike test.
[06:33] Olivia: does the console give per-route dashboards so platform can auto-alert on token regressions?
[06:39] Maya: the Console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level billing breakdown, latency histograms, and alert rules. you can also export traces to jaeger or use our tracing hooks.
[06:48] Mateo: any caveats around streaming responses and function/tool calls? we use streaming for better UX.
[06:55] Jamal: streaming is supported. function-calls and structured outputs are supported but you should test edge cases like mid-stream reconnects — we have client libraries that handle resumes. one caveat: streaming latencies and token accounting can vary depending on your batch size and kernel optimizations.
[07:12] Olivia: curious about rate-limiting UX — can the gateway automatically fallback to a cheaper model when a tenant hits quota?
[07:19] Jamal: yes. policy rules allow fallback to model variants, reduce max tokens, or return degraded responses. rules can be as granular as tenant or route.
[07:27] Samir: any mention of competitor lock-in? we want portability.
[07:31] Maya: we try to avoid lock-in — SDKs are thin and the APIs align with open model interfaces. we support export of billing and model snapshots. Plus, you can run a Private deployment to keep everything in your VPC.
[07:44] Mateo: ok can you send sample LangChain adapter code? also we use LlamaIndex 0.8 — compatibility?
[07:50] Jamal: yes. we'll include a small adapter for LlamaIndex 0.8 and notes on streaming + embeddings.
[07:57] Olivia: procurement question — do you do SOC 2 Type II?
[08:01] Maya: yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation are available; i'll attach certs. also we support SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO.
[08:10] Samir: good. if we start hosted on a subset of traffic, what's the expected invoicing cadence and egress controls?
[08:17] Maya: billing is monthly by default; we can do committed spend for Dedicated. for egress you can restrict endpoints using network policies and we can do VPC peering for private flows.
[08:29] Olivia: wrap up — sounds promising. next steps: we want the security docs and SDK repos, jamal's benchmark plan, and we'll share expected QPS. can we lock a workshop week of 5/17?
[08:39] Maya: yes. i'll send a calendar invite for a 90-min architecture workshop for 5/18 to be safe.
[08:45] Mateo: quick note — i'll add our LangChain prompt sets to the shared drive so you can see prompt variability.
[08:50] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone.
[08:53] Jamal: thanks, bye.
[08:55] Recording end. This transcript contains typical auto-transcription noise: occasional mis-attributed speakers and minor word swaps.
